text:
The biggest story in Detroit this season is finished: Dylan Larkin asked out, and he got his wish. He is now a Canadien, and NHL.com covered his Montreal debut last weekend. The Red Wings are left sorting through the return, which Dimitri Filipovic's PDOcast described as extra draft capital, and the trade questions haven't stopped there, with Simon Edvinsson's name now in the rumor mill. It's a strange time to be a Red Wings fan.

On the ice, Detroit has been leaning hard on one man. Daniil Tarasov is at .930 and 11.63 goals saved above expected this season (goals he has stopped beyond what an average goalie would on the same shots), and .933 over his last five starts. He needs to be: the Red Wings didn't win the chance battle in any of their last five games, taking 40% of the expected goals, even in Wednesday's 5-1 win over Vancouver.

Columbus has the opposite problem. The Blue Jackets have created enough to be closer to even, but their finishing has cost them 10.8 goals against what their chances usually produce, and Jet Greaves sits at .875. Zach Werenski is the exception, with 9 points in 10 games and another franchise record, and Matthew Knies has been a big part of the story since arriving from Toronto. Denton Mateychuk is out. Adam Fantilli is our sleeper for a point at 53%, with his ice time up to a projected 21:59.

Our numbers expect a tight, low-event night: 2.99 goals for Columbus, 2.76 for Detroit. Both teams are on the outside, the Red Wings at 13% for the playoffs and the Blue Jackets at 8%. Michael Rasmussen, on the fourth line, is Detroit's sleeper at 12% to score. Kent Johnson is one assist from 100.
headline: The Red Wings' first stretch without Larkin
